info.title: DeepSearch API
info.summary: Programmatic people research from public sources.
info.description:
The DeepSearch API lets AI agents and applications research a person's PUBLIC online footprint.
Look someone up by name, phone, email, or username; build a full sourced dossier (social accounts,
contact details, work history, relatives, and web mentions); and ask follow-up questions.

Public information only. Authenticate with a bearer API key created in the developer portal.
Usage is metered against one weekly allowance shared with the app, MCP, CLI, and SDKs.
Each request settles from the model tokens and paid tools it actually uses. Cached results and idempotent replays are free.
After included usage is exhausted, non-expiring extra credits are used automatically without unlocking plan-restricted capabilities.

API and MCP billing is user-managed: DeepSearch uses account credentials for these routes. Standalone MPP research accepts caller-owned payment transports. If an API request returns
401 or 402, the error body includes an `action`, a `url`, and a `message` written for the agent to
relay to its user - direct the user to that URL to sign up, subscribe, or add credits, then retry.

## Try it without an account

Send `Authorization: Bearer dsk_test_deepsearch` and every response is a deterministic
fixture: the production envelope, headers and error contract, with a fixed payload. Nothing
is metered, no account is needed, and no production data is touched. Any key beginning
`dsk_test_` behaves the same way. With your own key, add `"sandbox": true`
to a request body instead. GET https://deepsearch.app/api/v1/sandbox describes the whole contract.

## Versioning and deprecation

The version is in the URL path (`/api/v1/...`). Within a version, changes are additive only:
new endpoints, new optional request fields, and new response fields. Adding a response field is
not a breaking change, so parse defensively and ignore what you do not recognise.

A breaking change ships as a new path version; `/api/v1` is never repurposed. When an operation
is deprecated it keeps working and starts sending two headers: `Deprecation`, the date the
decision was announced, and `Sunset`, the earliest date it may stop responding. Sunset is never
less than 12 months after Deprecation, the operation is marked `deprecated: true` in this
document, and the change is listed at https://deepsearch.app/changelog and in GET /api/developer/changelog.
An agent that watches for a `Sunset` header has at least a year to migrate.

post.summary: Build a full public-footprint profile for a person.
post.description: Pass a candidate from /search (or a minimal person object) and stream a structured dossier - identity, contact, social accounts, locations, work, mentions and a written summary with cited sources. Reports are cached privately for each account: repeating the same request from the same account replays the cached report instantly and consumes no usage. Reports are not shared between accounts.

Executes several search / dossier / chat operations in a single round trip.

Batching changes the transport and nothing else. Every item is authenticated by the
same key, checked against the same scope, counted against the same per-operation rate
limit, served from the same dossier cache, and billed exactly as it would have been on
its own - each item settles from the provider work it actually performs, while cached dossiers remain free. Items run sequentially.

A batch of 10 is the maximum; queue anything larger, or
anything slow, with POST /api/v1/jobs.

every item failed: each result carries its own status and its own error body. An
`Idempotency-Key` is extended per item (`<key>:<id>`), so retrying a partially failed
batch replays the items that succeeded instead of re-charging them.

get.description:
Returns the caller's async API jobs, newest first, in cursor pages.

Page by passing the previous response's `next_cursor` back as `cursor`. `has_more` is false and `next_cursor` is null on the last page, so an agent can loop until `has_more` is false without a separate count. Cursors are opaque: treat them as strings and do not construct one yourself.

parameters.description: Jobs per page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor`.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. Null on the last page.

has_more.description: Whether another page exists after this one.

operations.description: Each supported operation, with the exact fixture events it returns.

BatchRequest.description: 1 to 10 operations, as an object or a bare array.

usage.description: Batch totals. Per-item cost is in each result's own `usage`.

status.description: The HTTP status this item would have returned on its own. 504 means the batch ran out of time before the item started, so it was neither executed nor billed.

credits.description: Compatibility value for API v1; use percentageCharged.

SocialEvidenceEvent.description: Additive social-discovery event. Clients may ignore this family if they only need final hits.

UsageSettlementEvent.description: Authoritative post-run usage settlement. For SSE responses this event supersedes the provisional usage headers sent before provider work began.

addresses.description: Approximate / public-record locations only - never precise

message.description: A human-readable explanation. On 401/402 it is phrased for the agent to relay to its user.

action.description: Present on onboarding-gated errors (401/402): the agent should send the user to `url`.

url.description: Where to direct the user (sign-in required).

docs_url.description: Public API overview the agent can also share.
